start_here_runtime: 57 minutes with the full response; 55–60 with normal variation. The manuscript is 6,840 words at about 120 words per minute.
start_here_cut: If you have 50 minutes: Introduction to 4, Movement 1 to 6, Movement 2 to 6, Movement 4 to 7, Application to 6. Keep the vessels, the hand, “weighed and found wanting,” and the gospel turn. Never cut the hand writing, Daniel’s refusal, or the cross.
start_here_guardrails: Do not cartoon Belshazzar. He is a warned man who knew the family record and refused to humble himself.
Keep the history honest: Belshazzar was a co-regent, “father” is dynastic language, and Darius the Mede’s identity is debated.
The temple vessels were holy because God claimed them, not because gold has magic.
Do not use Daniel’s refusal of gifts to attack all payment for ministry; the point is the price, not the salary.
Do not equate the Lord’s Supper with Belshazzar’s feast. Protect the hand, the refusal, the verdict, and the cross.
start_here_evidence: The co-regency of Belshazzar, the temple vessels, the handwriting, and the fall of Babylon to Cyrus in 539 BC are doing theological work.

slides.run: A SERMON FOR THE PULPIT · 55–60 MINUTES

slides.label: 01 · THE BIG IDEA
lines: A king held the vessels of God.
The God who held his breath
slides.note: The room was full of gold. The scale was empty.

slides.label: 03 · THE HAND
slides.headline: The room went silent.

columns.note: The God who is spirit writes with fingers.
In the light, where no one could miss it.
The king’s body preached the truth.

panel: The room that owned the night
could not hold its king upright.

slides.label: 04 · THE VERDICT
slides.headline: The scale no gold could tip.
slides.body: The king had a thousand lords, the temple’s gold, and a title. On God’s scale, none of it had weight. The verdict was not “try harder.” It was “found wanting.”
slides.pullquote: All the gold in the room had no weight on that scale.
slides.footline: The sentence was already written before the king knew his name was in it.

slides.label: 05 · THE REFUSAL
slides.headline: The prophet would not be bought.
slides.quote: “Let your gifts be for yourself... Nevertheless, I will read the writing.”
slides.aside1: He refused the reward, not the task.
slides.aside2: The word of God is not a product. The prophet is not a performer.
slides.footline: “Let your gifts be for yourself.” — Daniel 5:17

slides.label: 07 · THE GOSPEL
slides.banner_main: “This he set aside, nailing it to the cross.”
lines: The sentence we deserved fell on him.
The verdict was not canceled; it was carried.
slides.footline: The writing on the wall was a sentence. The writing on the cross is a pardon.

slides.label: 08 · THE TRUE KING
slides.banner_main: “For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin.”
lines: The King who had all weight became weightless for us.
slides.footline: The scale did not go away. It went to the cross.

slides.label: 09 · THE RESPONSE
slides.headline: What do you do with the weight?

title: Stop decorating
with the sacred.
items.desc: The vessels were holy. The party was not. Do not use God’s things for your own glory.

title: Read the
handwriting.
items.desc: You already have warnings, Scripture, and consequences. Do not wait for a hand on the wall.

title: Do not buy
the verdict.
items.desc: Purple and gold cannot purchase truth. Come empty-handed.

title: Number
your days.
items.desc: The party is not forever. Wisdom weighs the time it has.

slides.footline: The scale is not your neighbor’s life. It is the glory of God.

slides.label: 10 · THE INVITATION
slides.line1: Not clean up the party. Not buy the sentence. Come.
lines: The writing on the wall was a sentence.
